entities.name: CBS Sports
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
CBS Sports, the sports division of the CBS television network — home since 1956 to major American sports broadcasting including the NFL (current rights to AFC games), NCAA March Madness basketball tournament, Masters golf, PGA Championship, the US Open tennis tournament, and formerly the NBA and MLB — is one of the most historically significant sports broadcasting organizations in American media history, responsible for landmark sports television moments and for shaping the role of sports in American broadcast television culture.

CBS Sports' golden era spanned the 1960s-1980s: the network's NFL coverage with iconic announcers including Phyllis George, Pat Summerall, and John Madden (who became the defining NFL voice through his CBS, Fox, and NBC stints), its early Super Bowl broadcasts, and its famous Wide World of Sports-era sports anthology programming established the cultural template for sports television. The NFL relationship — the most commercially valuable in American sports television — has been CBS's most important partnership across six decades.

CBS Sports' March Madness coverage (since 1982, extended through a deal with Turner) is the network's most emotionally significant annual programming: the NCAA Basketball Tournament's 64-team bracket, Cinderella stories, and 'One Shining Moment' finale have become one of American sports culture's most beloved traditions. CBS's golf coverage including the Masters and PGA Championship maintains the highest production standards in golf broadcasting. CBS Sports Network (cable) and Paramount+ streaming have extended the brand into new distribution channels. Jim Nantz remains one of television sports broadcasting's most respected voices.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: CBS Sports — broadcasting Super Bowls, shaping March Madness culture, housing John Madden's defining color commentary, and maintaining the Masters and NFL as cornerstone American sports television properties — is one of the most historically significant sports broadcasting institutions in American media.
